thread_analysis.thread_summary: [COMPANY] (a keyboard manufacturer) works with [COMPANY] to certify a keyboard via HOGP profile testing, referencing an existing HID Input Devices registration. The thread covers a registration-system change that now makes BAS, DIS, and HIDS mandatory minimum-item testing a cascading requirement of any HOGP-Device role registration, a customer request for a workaround when some of those new mandatory items returned Fail/Indecisive, and a detailed troubleshooting episode on a BAS Battery Level change-notification test item that initially failed due to a mismatch between the test's voltage ramp rate and the device's battery-level detection/reporting interval, eventually resolved by timing the voltage step-down to a PTS prompt.
all_questions_found: What information (company details for the test report, HOGP/BAS/DIS/HIDS ICS support details, and a brief operation manual) does the customer need to submit alongside the test sample for profile testing?
Given the existing registration already includes HOGP, are there any ICS changes or additions needed for the current registration, beyond the new mandatory BAS/DIS/HIDS minimum items?
Is the new BAS/DIS/HIDS minimum-item testing now a mandatory cascading requirement of any HOGP-Device role registration, regardless of whether the product was previously registered without them?
If this round's Fail/Indecisive test items aren't passed, can the certification registration still be completed?
Is there any way around needing to pass the BAS/DIS/HIDS items that came back Fail or Indecisive, short of fixing the firmware to genuinely pass them?

If the existing pre-BAS/DIS/HIDS registration hasn't had market connectivity-compatibility problems, does that mean the product doesn't actually rely on those profiles' functionality, and could a different company's existing Profile Subsystem registration be referenced instead?

Why does the BAS Battery Level change-notification test item fail when the test voltage is lowered steadily from 5.1V, with the DUT powering off abruptly around 2.8V instead of properly reporting a battery-level change?
What are the customer's actual voltage threshold levels and detection period for the battery-level indicator (e.g., the 30%/10% thresholds) needed to inform retesting?
Does timing the voltage step-down to coincide with PTS's on-screen prompt to change the battery level, rather than a steady ramp, resolve the BAS Battery Level test item?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread covers two technical threads: first, a registration-system change that makes BAS, DIS, and HIDS minimum-item testing a cascading requirement for any HOGP-Device role registration, with a documented workaround of referencing an existing third-party Profile Subsystem registration that already includes those profiles, usable when the product doesn't functionally depend on them and as a last resort rather than a first choice. Second, a BAS Battery Level change-notification test item that initially failed because the test's steady voltage ramp-down was faster than the DUT's battery-level detection/reporting interval, causing the DUT to miss reporting the intermediate threshold and instead power off; the fix was to time the voltage step-down to PTS's on-screen prompt rather than a fixed steady ramp.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: When a HOGP-Device role registration now requires BAS/DIS/HIDS minimum items that the product's firmware does not pass, the recommended priority is to first attempt a firmware fix to genuinely pass the minimum items, and only fall back to referencing an existing third-party Profile Subsystem registration that already covers those profiles if the product can be shown not to functionally depend on them (e.g., no known market compatibility issues from an existing registration that lacked them). For the Battery Level test, the deciding insight is that a fixed-rate voltage ramp can outpace a device's own battery-level detection/reporting interval, so the correct test technique is to step the voltage down only when the test system's own prompt indicates it is checking for that specific change, rather than a continuous steady decline.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming the new mandatory BAS/DIS/HIDS testing could be skipped or that the prior, pre-change registration's scope still applied would block certification registration entirely, since the Fail/Indecisive items must be passed (or addressed via the Profile Subsystem reference workaround) before registration can proceed. Continuing to test the Battery Level item with a steady voltage ramp without recognizing the detection-interval mismatch risked repeated false failures and wasted retest cycles.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a registration-system change introduces a new cascading minimum-item requirement (such as BAS/DIS/HIDS under HOGP-Device role), check whether the product's prior registration scope and market history already demonstrate it doesn't rely on the newly-required profiles before recommending a reference-based workaround, and treat that workaround as a last resort behind a genuine firmware fix. Separately, when a test item involves a changing physical condition (such as a battery-level threshold) and a steady test ramp doesn't reproduce the expected DUT behavior, consider whether the DUT's own detection/reporting timing is being outpaced by the ramp rate, and align the test's timing to the DUT's or test system's own signal rather than a fixed rate.
